topic: Aerodrome signals, markings and lighting (Skyway Code)
summary: Ground signals sit in the signal square: a white or orange T shows the landing direction, a right-hand arrow means right-hand circuits, and a red square with one yellow diagonal means special precautions. Two yellow diagonals mean landings are prohibited, a white dumb-bell means use runways and taxiways only. Mandatory signs are white on red and you must not pass them without clearance or checking the runway. A red stop bar must never be crossed. APAPI: one white and one red light on the correct slope. Built from the Skyway Code pp.107-113.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), pp.107-113
sections: Signal square
White or orange T: land and take off parallel to the shaft of the T, towards the cross arm
Right-hand arrow: turns to the right before landing and after take-off. Absent any signal, left-hand circuits are the norm
Red square with one yellow diagonal: special precautions in approaching or landing, for example poor state of the manoeuvring area
Red square with two yellow diagonals: landings prohibited
Horizontal white dumb-bell: land, take off and taxi on runways and taxiways only
Dumb-bell with black stripes: take-offs and landings on runways only, other manoeuvres need not be
Double white cross: gliding operations in progress
Cross on the surface: area unfit for aircraft (white on a runway, yellow on a taxiway)
Black C on yellow: where a pilot reports to ATC or the person in charge. Visiting pilots usually report here
Runway lighting and PAPI
Typical GA runway: green threshold lights, white edge lights, red end lights
A simple approach lighting system is a single white T-bar to help acquire the runway in poor visibility
PAPI shows whether you are on the correct approach angle, normally between 3° and 4°
Most GA aerodromes have a two-light APAPI: on the correct slope one light is white and one is red. Larger aerodromes typically use four lights
Taxiway signs and holding points
Taxiways are named by a letter such as Alpha. Holding points are usually a letter and number

Mandatory instruction signs are white on red. Do not pass one without permission from ATC (controlled aerodrome), or at an uncontrolled aerodrome without checking the runway and final approach are clear and announcing your intentions
The holding position marking on the ground has two solid yellow lines followed by two dashed lines on the runway side
Guard lights are pairs of alternately flashing yellow lights at the holding point
Stop bars at larger controlled aerodromes are red lights across the taxiway. Never cross a red stop bar. ATC switches it off and the green lights beyond come on after clearance to cross or enter
Hot spots on charts are holding points prone to runway incursions
Marshalling
A marshaller may direct you to park at larger aerodromes. Details are in Appendix 1 of SERA and CAP 637
Normal stop: arms and wands extended at 90° moved slowly above the head until they cross. Emergency stop: abruptly extend arms and wands to the top of the head, crossing wands
Wands pointing up with arms raised means identify gate

sum.Signal square: T, arrows, red squares, dumb-bells and crosses.

cards.q: What does a white or orange T mean?
cards.a: Land and take off parallel to the shaft towards the cross arm.

cards.q: What does a right-hand arrow in the signal square mean?
cards.a: Right-hand circuits. Left-hand is the norm otherwise.

cards.q: Red square with one yellow diagonal?
cards.a: Take special precautions in approaching or landing.

cards.q: Red square with two yellow diagonals?

cards.a: Land, take off and taxi on runways and taxiways only.

cards.q: Cross on the surface, and its colours?
cards.a: Area unfit for movement: white on runways, yellow on taxiways.
Where to report to ATC or the person in charge.
Green threshold, white edge, red end.

cards.q: Normal approach angle indicated by PAPI?

cards.a: One white light and one red light.
White letters on a red background.
Two solid yellow lines then two dashed lines on the runway side.

cards.q: Can you cross a red stop bar?
cards.a: Never. Wait for ATC to switch it off.

quiz.q: A red square with two yellow diagonals in the signal square means:
quiz.why: Two diagonals mean landings are prohibited.

quiz.q: On the correct slope a two-light APAPI shows:
quiz.why: One white and one red light indicate the correct approach path.
They mark runway entry points and must not be passed without permission.

quiz.q: You are approaching a red stop bar. You should:
o: Stop and wait for ATC to switch it off
Cross if the runway looks clear
quiz.why: Never cross a red stop bar.

quiz.q: A white or orange T shows:
quiz.why: Aircraft land and take off parallel to the shaft towards the cross arm.
Gliding is taking place at the aerodrome.
